=== NEW MEMBER, minimised s399 (the biggest single cause) =================

A PARENLESS user-sub call whose FIRST argument is a NAMED UNARY, followed by a
low-precedence `or`/`and`, is dropped whole:

    sub f { print "f(@_)\n"; 0 }   sub g { print "g(@_)\n"; 1 }   my $u = "x";

    f ref $u, "m", "d" or g "fb";   perl: f( m d) g(fb)   PCL: (nothing)
    f ref $u or g "fb";             perl: f() g(fb)       PCL: (nothing)
    f ref $u, "m" and g "fb";       perl: f( m)           PCL: (nothing)
  INVERSE (both work today):
    f $u, "m", "d" or g "fb";       identical            <- no named unary
    f(ref $u, "m") or g "fb";       identical            <- parenthesised

So the trigger is (parenless call) x (named-unary first argument) x (low-prec
`or`/`and` after).  That is `Test::More`'s `is … or diag $@` idiom, which is
why it shows up in perl-tests files.

=== MECHANISM LOCATED AND MEASURED s417 â docs/b2-stale-operand-ceiling-s417.md ===

The plan's "take this DIFF first" was taken.  The mechanism is a STALE INDEX,
not a grammar gap:

  handle_subcalls scans @$e RIGHT TO LEFT and saves `$last_low_prio_op = $i`
  when it passes an and/or/xor (PExpr.pm ~3575).  The same scan then REDUCES
  words to its left, splicing @$e and shifting that operator LEFT â and the
  saved index is never adjusted.  The paren-less list operator then computes
  `$end_pars = $last_low_prio_op - 1` (~3758) from a position that no longer
  means what it meant, so its argument list runs past the operator that should
  have ended it.

  f $u     or g "fb"   -> or at 2, saved 2, end_pars 1   CORRECT
  f ref $u or g "fb"   -> or at 2, saved 3, end_pars 2 = the `or`  SWALLOWED

The error is (elements the intervening reduction consumed - 1), so it is NOT
always off-by-one: `f ref $h{k} or g "fb"` is off by TWO.

THE FAMILY HAS AN UNCOUNTED HALF.  With a larger shift the statement does not
drop â it RUNS with the `or` swallowed:

  f ref $h{k} or g "fb";     perl: f() g(fb)      PCL: g(fb) f(1)

so the drop census can only ever see part of this task.

POPULATION SCAN (PCL_B2_TRACE=1, the probe added s417, 658 files both
populations, 1m34s): 10 events, 3 distinct sources â
  * bless.t:179 `is ref $untied, "main", 'â¦' or diag $@`  = the census DROP
  * split.t:503 `my ($sp) = grep â¦, map chr, reverse â¦ or skip â¦`
        = a SILENT WRONG in NO count (probed: perl runs the `or` branch,
          PCL does not)
  * t/re/reg_fold.t:165 `eval join â¦ or die $@` = stale index, BENIGN emission
        (probed identical to perl) â so a disagreement is NECESSARY BUT NOT
        SUFFICIENT for a divergence, and any gate built on the probe must
        probe each site rather than trust it.

The words involved are not only user subs: `map` and `eval` fire too, so this
task's framing ("a parenless USER-sub call") is narrower than the mechanism.

$end_pars GRAMMAR change â see Â§4 of the doc.
